title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Implicit hypothesis: the identification of the geometric groups π for U_{K̄} and U_{k̄}, and of inertia with T, holds only for the prime-to-p (or tame) quotient when char k(s) = p > 0. The page writes π throughout without stating this restriction.
The isomorphism E_{U_s} → E_{U_Õ} requires U/S to be a good relative curve near s: X smooth proper and the cusp divisor étale over S. This is assumed tacitly.

ideas.what: With non-strict henselization at a codimension-1 point, the arithmetic fundamental extension of U_Õ is canonically the extension (27) of the special fibre U_s over k(s).
ideas.modern_name: Specialization of (tame) fundamental groups / Grothendieck specialization isomorphism
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. X and XIII; Grothendieck–Murre LNM 208

ideas.what: A rational point over the henselian fraction field gives a section of the middle row, equivalently a lift λ of D_s → Gal(k(s)) into E_{U_s}.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stix (log-étale specialization of sections, ~2002; book 'Rational points and arithmetic of fundamental groups' 2013)
ideas.where_published: Possibly in the Malgoire edition of La Longue Marche; letter to Faltings (1983) only sketches the section conjecture

ideas.what: Criterion: the section is non-regular at s (the point reduces to a cusp) iff λ is nontrivial on inertia iff λ|I = k_i∘(μ·), where μ is the contact multiplicity with the cusp. The decomposition group then sits with index μ in the normalizer of the cusp inertia.
ideas.modern_name: Cuspidal sections / sections at the boundary (packets at cusps)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's letter to Faltings mentions sections attached to cusps; details not published

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up machinery to specialize sections at codimension-1 points of an arbitrary base S. This points to an induction on transcendence degree for the section conjecture over finitely generated fields, with cuspidal degeneration controlled by the inertia multiplicity μ. A general reduction of the section conjecture for finitely generated fields to number fields along these lines is not, as far as I know, established in the literature.
missed.quote: La situation de la courbe relative U/S, et d'un s∈S de codim 1, définit par hensélisation (pas stricte) en s le diagramme (26)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a concrete strategy for dévissage of the section conjecture from finitely generated fields to number fields. The individual ingredients are known, but the global induction remains open.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful early working-out of specialization and cuspidal behaviour of Galois sections, with the multiplicity μ. This anticipates work of Nakamura, Stix and Hoshi, but the individual statements are now standard in anabelian geometry.
transcription_corrections: 'hensélisation ({+pas+} [-stricte-])' should read 'hensélisation (pas stricte)': 'pas' is inserted above 'stricte', which is not deleted. The meaning is the non-strict henselization, consistent with E_Õ ≅ E_{k(s)}.
In the parenthesis, the inserted text reads roughly 'l'hom. sur les π_1 correspondant' replacing the crossed-out 'l'inclusion'.
'Une section rationnelle f/ de U sur S' is written as an insertion above the line: 'f' with a slash.
